title: Create a GitHub Repository
description: Learn how to create a new remote repository on GitHub to store and share your code.

steps.title: Log in to GitHub
steps.instruction: Open your web browser and navigate to GitHub. Sign in to your account, or click 'Sign up' if you don't have an account yet.
steps.result: You will be on your GitHub dashboard.
steps.mistake: Creating a repo without signing in first or forgetting your login credentials.

steps.title: Create a New Repository
steps.instruction: In the upper-right corner of any page, click the '+' icon and select 'New repository'. Alternatively, click the green 'New' button on your dashboard.
steps.result: Opens the 'Create a new repository' setup page.
steps.mistake: Naming the repo with spaces or special symbols instead of kebab-case (e.g. my-project).

steps.title: Configure Repository Settings
steps.instruction: Enter a short, memorable repository name. Choose Public (anyone can see it) or Private. Leave 'Add a README file' UNCHECKED if you are uploading an existing local project.
steps.result: Repository is created and GitHub displays your unique clone/push URL.
steps.warning: If you check 'Add a README' when you already have code locally, you will encounter merge conflicts on your first push!
steps.mistake: Checking 'Add a README' or '.gitignore' when importing an existing local folder.

steps.title: Copy Your Repository URL
steps.instruction: Copy the HTTPS URL shown on the quick-setup page. It will look like https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/YOUR-REPO.git.
steps.result: URL copied to clipboard for use in terminal commands.
steps.warning: Remember to replace YOUR-USERNAME and YOUR-REPO with your actual GitHub username and repository name!

title: Connect a Local Project to GitHub
description: Link an existing project folder on your computer to your remote GitHub repository.

steps.title: Open Terminal & Navigate to Project
steps.instruction: Open Command Prompt, PowerShell, or Git Bash, and navigate into your project folder.
steps.result: Your terminal prompt shows your project directory.
steps.mistake: Running commands from Desktop or User home directory instead of inside the project folder.

steps.title: Initialize Git Repository
steps.instruction: Initialize a new Git repository in the current directory if you haven't already.
steps.result: Initialized empty Git repository in .../.git/
steps.mistake: Running git init multiple times in parent and subfolders.

steps.title: Add Remote Origin
steps.instruction: Connect your local Git repository to your GitHub remote. Replace the URL with your actual GitHub repository URL.
steps.result: Local Git now knows where 'origin' points.
steps.warning: Replace 'YOUR-USERNAME' and 'YOUR-REPO' with your real GitHub details!
steps.mistake: Pasting the example URL directly without replacing username and repo name.

steps.title: Verify Connection
steps.instruction: Check that the remote URL was set correctly.
steps.result:
origin  https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/YOUR-REPO.git (fetch)
origin  https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/YOUR-REPO.git (push)
steps.mistake: If you see 'fatal: remote origin already exists', use: git remote set-url origin <url>

title: Upload Code for the First Time
description: Stage your files, commit your initial snapshot, set main branch, and push your code to GitHub.

steps.title: Check Repository Status
steps.instruction: Inspect which files are untracked and modified.
steps.result: Displays list of untracked files in red.
steps.mistake: Forgetting to create a .gitignore file before staging secrets or node_modules.

steps.title: Stage All Files
steps.instruction: Stage all files in the current folder for the first commit.
steps.result: All files move to the staging area (ready to be committed).
steps.mistake: Staging massive binary files, virtual environments (.venv), or node_modules.

steps.title: Commit Your Changes
steps.instruction: Save the snapshot with a meaningful commit message.
steps.code: git commit -m "Initial commit: Project setup and starter files"
steps.result: [main (root-commit) 7a1b2c3] Initial commit: ...
steps.mistake: Using vague messages like 'asdf' or 'update'.

steps.title: Rename Default Branch to Main
steps.instruction: Ensure your default branch is named 'main' to match modern GitHub standards.
steps.result: Current branch renamed to 'main'.
steps.mistake: Pushing to 'master' when GitHub repository expects 'main'.

steps.title: Push to GitHub (Set Upstream)
steps.instruction: Push your local commits to origin main and set tracking.
steps.result: Branch 'main' set up to track remote branch 'main' from 'origin'. Your code is live on GitHub!
steps.mistake: If prompted for authentication, GitHub requires a Personal Access Token (PAT) or SSH key, not your account password.

title: Push Subsequent Changes
description: Learn the everyday development loop: make changes, stage them, commit, and push updates to GitHub.

steps.title: Check Modified Files
steps.instruction: View what has changed since your last commit.
steps.result: Shows modified files in red under 'Changes not staged for commit'.
steps.mistake: Not checking git status before staging to review what you changed.

steps.title: Inspect Line Diffs (Optional)
steps.instruction: See exact line additions and deletions before staging.
steps.result: Green '+' lines indicate additions, red '-' lines indicate removals.
steps.mistake: Overlooking accidental console.log or temporary test code.

steps.title: Stage and Commit
steps.instruction: Stage your changes and commit with a concise, descriptive message.
steps.code:
git add .
git commit -m "Add navigation bar and responsive styling"
steps.result: Files committed to your local Git history.
steps.mistake: Grouping unrelated features into one giant commit.

steps.title: Push to Remote
steps.instruction: Send your new commits to GitHub. Since upstream was set previously, you can simply run git push.
steps.result: Counting objects... Writing objects: 100%... Successfully pushed to origin/main.
steps.mistake: If push is rejected, run 'git pull' first to fetch remote updates.

title: Create and Switch Branches
description: Isolate new features and bug fixes by creating independent branches without affecting production code.

steps.title: List Existing Branches
steps.instruction: See all local branches and which one is currently active (marked with an asterisk *).
steps.result: * main
steps.mistake: Branching off an outdated branch instead of pulling main first.

steps.title: Create and Switch to a Feature Branch
steps.instruction: Use 'git switch -c' (modern) or 'git checkout -b' to create and immediately switch to a new branch.
steps.result: Switched to a new branch 'feature-auth-system'
steps.mistake: Using spaces in branch names. Use hyphens like feature-login or bugfix-header.

steps.title: Work and Commit on the Branch
steps.instruction: Make your edits freely. Changes will only affect this feature branch.
steps.code:
git add .
git commit -m "Implement JWT token verification"
steps.result: [feature-auth-system 3b8c4d1] Implement JWT token verification
steps.mistake: Switching branches with unstaged dirty work. Use 'git stash' if needed.

steps.title: Push Feature Branch to GitHub
steps.instruction: Publish your branch to GitHub so colleagues can review it or build on it.
steps.result: Branch 'feature-auth-system' created on GitHub.
steps.mistake: Forgetting the '-u origin <branch>' on the first push of a new branch.

title: Create a Pull Request (PR)
description: Propose merging your feature branch into main with team peer review and automated testing.

steps.title: Push Your Branch to GitHub
steps.instruction: Make sure all your latest commits are pushed to the remote branch.
steps.result: GitHub receives all latest commits for the branch.
steps.mistake: Forgetting to push your final commits before opening the PR.

steps.title: Open Pull Request on GitHub
steps.instruction: Visit your repository on GitHub. You'll see a yellow banner: 'feature-auth-system had recent pushes'. Click 'Compare & pull request'.
steps.result: Opens the Pull Request creation form.
steps.mistake: Comparing against the wrong base branch (ensure base: main <- compare: feature-branch).

steps.title: Write Description & Submit
steps.instruction: Provide a clear summary of what changes were made, why, and how to test them.
steps.code:
## Summary
- Added user authentication endpoints
- Integrated token refresh

## Testing
- Tested with Postman & unit tests
steps.result: Pull request is opened, assigned reviewers get notified, and CI checks run.
steps.mistake: Leaving PR title and description completely empty.

steps.title: Merge Pull Request
steps.instruction: Once approved, click 'Merge pull request' -> 'Confirm merge'. On your local machine, switch back to main and pull the merged changes.
steps.code:
git switch main
git pull origin main
git branch -d feature-auth-system
steps.result: Local main is now updated with the merged changes, and the feature branch is cleaned up.
steps.mistake: Continuing to develop on the old feature branch after it has already been merged.

title: Resolve a Merge Conflict
description: Understand why merge conflicts happen and follow safe, step-by-step resolution without losing work.

steps.title: Identify the Conflict
steps.instruction: When Git cannot automatically combine two changes to the same line, it alerts you with CONFLICT.
steps.code:
git pull origin main
# CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in index.html
# Automatic merge failed; fix conflicts and then commit the result.
steps.result: Git pauses the merge and marks conflicting files.
steps.mistake: Panicking or deleting files. Conflicts are a completely normal part of team development!

steps.title: Inspect Conflict Markers in Editor
steps.instruction: Open the conflicting file in VS Code or your editor. Look for conflict markers:
steps.code:
<<<<<<< HEAD

My Local Title

=======

Team Remote Title

>>>>>>> origin/main
steps.result: HEAD represents your local changes; the bottom part represents incoming changes from remote.
steps.mistake: Leaving '<<<<<<<', '=======', or '>>>>>>>' markers in your code.

steps.title: Choose & Edit Desired Code
steps.instruction: Manually edit the file to keep the desired code (or combine both). Delete all three conflict marker lines.
steps.code: Git & GitHub Assistant — Your Intelligent Coding Companion
steps.result: The file contains clean, valid code without any marker syntax.
steps.mistake: Accidentally deleting closing tags, semicolons, or braces while editing.

steps.title: Stage and Finalize Merge
steps.instruction: Stage the resolved file and commit to complete the merge.
steps.code:
git add index.html
git commit -m "Resolve merge conflict in index.html"
git push origin main
steps.result: Merge is successfully completed and pushed to GitHub!
steps.warning: If you ever get stuck or want to cancel the merge entirely, run: git merge --abort
steps.mistake: Running destructive commands like 'git reset --hard' which will delete all your uncommitted work!

title: Create a Professional README File
description: Structure a high-quality Markdown README.md file that showcases your project to visitors and recruiters.

steps.title: Create README.md File
steps.instruction: Create a new file named README.md in the root directory of your project.
steps.result: Empty README.md created in root directory.
steps.mistake: Creating readme.txt or Readme.doc instead of README.md with Markdown formatting.

steps.title: Add Title & Badges
steps.instruction: Start with a prominent title, tagline, and project badges.
steps.code:
# ⚡ Git & GitHub Assistant
> Your Intelligent Coding Companion

![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)
![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-brightgreen.svg)
steps.result: Visually appealing header on GitHub.
steps.mistake: Not providing a clear 1-2 sentence elevator pitch of what the app does.

steps.title: Include Features & Tech Stack
steps.instruction: List key capabilities and technologies used.
steps.code:
## ✨ Key Features
- 🤖 Interactive AI Chatbot
- ⌨️ Searchable Git Command Explorer
- 📖 Step-by-Step GitHub Tutorials
- 🔍 Git Error Troubleshooter

## 🛠️ Tech Stack
- Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript
- Backend: Python Flask
- AI: Google Gemini API & Local Fallback
steps.result: Clear structural overview for readers and evaluators.
steps.mistake: Listing vague features without explaining how to use the app.

steps.title: Add Installation & Usage Instructions
steps.instruction: Provide exact, copyable command snippets so anyone can run your project locally.
steps.code:
## 🚀 Quick Start
```bash
git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/gitmate-ai.git
cd gitmate-ai
pip install -r requirements.txt
python app.py
```
steps.result: Complete, working guide that anyone can clone and test.
steps.mistake: Assuming dependencies are already installed or omitting port information.

steps.title: Stage, Commit & Push
steps.instruction: Commit your README and push it to GitHub to see the formatted output immediately.
steps.code:
git add README.md
git commit -m "docs: Add comprehensive README.md with setup guide"
git push
steps.result: GitHub automatically renders README.md on the repository homepage.
steps.mistake: Not previewing markdown formatting before pushing.
